business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and 10-Q MD&A overview.
business_model.claim: The company buys portfolios of charged-off consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and collects on them. Its main asset classes are credit card, auto, utilities and telecom receivables.
quotes: The Company primarily purchases portfolios of consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and manages them by working with individuals as they repay their obligations and work toward financial recovery.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and the Item 1A risk factor.
business_model.claim: Sellers of the portfolios are creditors: banks, fintech platforms, telecom providers, card issuers and auto finance companies. Purchases are concentrated among a few of them, with the top five clients at 45.2% and 55.3% of purchases and the top client at 23.6% and 32.8% (years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024).
quotes: The Company’s top five clients accounted for 45.2% and 55.3%, with the top client representing 23.6% and 32.8% of purchases for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q and 10-K MD&A overviews.
business_model.claim: The company reports four geographic segments: United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Latin America. It also runs two lines of business, Distressed (the largest) and Insolvency.
quotes: We operate and manage our business through four reportable segments that are based on geography: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Latin America.
Distressed, our largest line of business, represents the purchase, collection, and servicing collection of nonperforming consumer loans

business_model.basis: stated in the segment table of the 10-K MD&A and the 8-K earnings release table.
business_model.claim: The United States is the dominant segment. For 2025 it had total revenue of $450.3 (table in millions) out of $613.3 million, against $50.8 (United Kingdom), $71.8 (Canada) and $40.4 (Latin America), all table in millions. U.S. ERC at September 30, 2026 was $2,586.0 (table in millions) of a total of $3.6 billion.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and the 10-K MD&A revenue description.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes mainly from portfolio revenue, with smaller credit card and servicing (fee-for-collection) revenue. In the nine months to September 30, 2026, total portfolio revenue was 502,598 of total revenues of 539,493, with credit card revenue of 4,984 and servicing revenue of 31,911 (all in thousands).
quotes: Servicing revenue consists of the revenue we generate from providing collection services to certain third parties.

business_model.basis: definition stated in the 10-K MD&A; amounts stated in the income statement.
business_model.claim: Portfolio revenue has two parts: portfolio income, which accretes at each pool's effective interest rate, and changes in recoveries, which reflect collections above or below forecast and revisions to expected future collections. In Q3 2026 portfolio income was 165,491 and changes in recoveries were 7,181 (thousands). For the nine months, changes in recoveries were 23,248 against 5,670 a year earlier.
quotes: Portfolio revenue consists of two components

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q MD&A, the earnings release and the income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by how much is deployed into new portfolios and how much is collected. In Q3 2026 the company invested $318.0 million, up 110.6% from $151.0 million, and collections were $319.2 million, up 34.8% from $236.8 million. Total revenues were 185,514 against 150,842 (thousands).
quotes: Deployments are a key driver of the growth of our ERC and a measure to compare growth in our business with the growth of other companies in the debt collection industry.

business_model.claim: The price paid relative to face value varies with the type and age of the accounts bought. Newly charged-off or paying portfolios cost more per dollar of face value. In Q3 2026 the average purchase price was 8.6% of face value against 5.3% a year earlier; for the nine months it was 6.7% against 6.1%.
quotes: The average purchase price as a percentage of face value is higher for newly charged-off portfolios as compared to more seasoned portfolios because newly charged-off portfolios generally have higher liquidation rates.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 Seasonality section.
business_model.claim: The business is seasonal. Deployments peak in the fourth quarter, when originators clear their books before year end. Collections are strongest from February to mid-April, when tax refunds are paid.
quotes: Our business typically experiences its busiest season in terms of deployments in the fourth quarter of the year.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement, the 10-K MD&A and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Servicing expense, the cost of collecting, is the largest operating cost. In Q3 2026 it was 67,737 of total operating expenses of 98,379 (thousands), against 47,609 a year earlier. The release attributes a $20.1 million increase to servicing, including $6.3 million of higher court costs.
quotes: Servicing expenses primarily consists of collections and customer service expenses associated with previously charged-off receivables, such as the cost of outsourced collections, debtor correspondence, legal fees associated with the collection of debt and other direct expenses associated with collections and customer service efforts.

business_model.basis: stated in the balance sheet, the income statement, the earnings release and the 8-K.
business_model.claim: The company funds purchases with debt, so interest is the second major cost. Notes payable were 1,538,195 (thousands) at September 30, 2026, and Q3 interest expense was 31,612 against 26,467. The leverage ratio was 1.73x against 1.59x. The company had $554 million drawn under the RCF and issued an additional $100 million of 8.250% Senior Notes due 2030 in August 2026.
quotes: Interest expense consists of interest expense on our outstanding debt and amortization of debt issuance costs.
At September 30, 2026, the Company had $554 million drawn under the RCF

business_model.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the funding link is inferred from the financing lines.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K, the 10-K risk factors and the earnings release.
